# Implementation Plan: codex-rebase-phase-5a-5b-ci-closeout

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-01 (autonomous mode). Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md --autonomous`.*

*v2: revised against 3-reviewer findings (Claude + Codex + Copilot). v1 archived as `draft-plan-v1.md` in the plan-review staging directory.*

## Overview

Make `cargo check --workspace` a hard, procedural Phase 5a gate in the
codex rebase skill, and establish Phase 5b as the post-push CI watch
that wraps every rebase commit. The 2026-05-30 `rust-v0.135.0` rebase
shipped without local cargo-check verification because the commit
message explicitly punted it to CI; the next week burned ~5 sequential
"rebase-debt-fix" Ralph members chasing compiler errors a 6-minute local
check would have caught. The lesson is already in
`plans/codexu-roadmap.md` Ship #41 and fork-level `AGENTS.md`, but as
advisory memory — it has to become procedural in the rebase skill itself
or future rebase agents will read the punt-to-CI precedent and repeat
it.

This plan is **doc-only**. No Rust code changes, no workflow YAML, no
new scripts. Five files in impl scope (rebase skill, two mirror
pointers in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.override.md, fork-level codexu
AGENTS.md cross-ref, `.ralph-overview/data.json` warnings update).
One post-ship file outside impl scope (`plans/codexu-roadmap.md` is
the bookkeeper's responsibility after merge).

The plan also documents the immediate CI-monitoring action implied by
the original task spec — which is **gated indefinitely** on the
operator-only `escalate-gim-home-actions-policy` task because every
recent `invariant-check` run on `gim-home/codex@main` returns
`startup_failure` with zero jobs (100/100 since 2026-04-07). Until that
unblocks, Phase 5b "interim closeout" is the only achievable state and
the protocol explicitly documents it as such — plus a concrete sunset
checklist the bookkeeper executes once the org policy lifts.

**CI ground truth** (`codex/.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml`):

- Trigger: `on: push: branches: [main, 'codex-patched/**']` (lines 3-7).

- Checkout uses `submodules: recursive`, so when a wrapper commit on

  triggers: `rust-ci` is PR-only, `rust-ci-full` is `push: branches:
  [main, **full-ci**]` and never fires on plain `sandbox-patches`
  pushes).

  `startup_failure` with empty `jobs` arrays** (verified via `gh run
  list` and `gh api .../actions/runs/...`). This is the canonical
  fingerprint of an org-level GitHub Actions policy rejection at
  dispatch time. The `escalate-gim-home-actions-policy` task documents
  this — operator-only fix at
  `https://github.com/organizations/gim-home/settings/actions`,
  blocking since at least 2026-04-07.

**The lesson source** (`plans/codexu-roadmap.md` lines 181-182, Ship
#41 "codex-rebase-debt lesson"): the verbatim policy text is the seed
for the Phase 5a section in the rebase skill — "Future rebase policy:
`cargo check --workspace` MUST run as a hard gate before sandbox-patches
push. Split into 'merge upstream (incomplete)' + 'post-merge
reconciliation (workspace green)' commits if needed."

````markdown
## Phase 5a — workspace cargo-check gate (HARD GATE before push)

**Phase 5a expands step 5; Phase 5b wraps steps 9-13.** Phase 5a runs
in the wrapper worktree's submodule checkout immediately after step
5's per-crate iteration loop converges and BEFORE step 6 commits +
force-pushes `sandbox-patches`. Phase 5a is a HARD GATE: do not push
the rebased sandbox-patches without it (or without the documented
split-commit fallback below).

### Why

The 2026-05-30 `rust-v0.135.0` rebase shipped with the commit message
`Full cargo check --workspace gate awaits a 1.95.0 install retry`,
which punted workspace-wide verification to CI. The week that followed
spent ~5 sequential rebase-debt-fix sessions on issues a workspace
cargo-check would have caught in 6 minutes: dangling fn refs, literal
git merge markers in `tui/src/style.rs`, missing `ConfigOverrides`
struct fields, missing `EventMsg::McpServerNotification` match arms
(including in code WE had written ourselves but never validated
workspace-wide). See `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` Ship #41 for the
post-mortem.

### Commands

Source the iteration env from the wrapper root (NOT relative to the
submodule cwd), then run the workspace check:

```bash
source "$REBASE_WORKTREE/scripts/iteration-env.sh"
cd "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs"
LOG="$REBASE_WORKTREE/.ralph/jobs/codex-upstream-rebase/cargo-check-workspace.out"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
cargo check --workspace 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
```

Wall-clock: ~6 minutes warm-cache on this workspace (per `CLAUDE.md`
build perf bullet); up to ~30 minutes cold if iteration env was just
sourced and sccache is empty.

### Exit gate

- **Zero compiler errors** (`error[E...]`) in the captured log.
  Warnings are tolerated and SHOULD be reviewed but do not block — they
  are upstream-imported in most cases.
- Final line must be `Finished ... profile in ...` (cargo's terminal
  success marker). If it ends with `error: could not compile ...`, the
  gate has not passed.
- The captured log path is recorded in the rebase task's
  `.ralph-overview/data.json` `shipManifest.summary` as verification
  evidence the rebase commit message can cite.

### What to do on failure

Each `error[E0xxx]` is rebase-debt. Resolve in the wrapper worktree's
submodule checkout (same place step 5 iterates):

- Missing struct field on initializer — add the upstream-introduced
  field with the upstream default value.
- Missing `match` arm on a fork-extended enum (e.g. `EventMsg::
  McpServerNotification`) — add the arm; default the behavior to the
  closest upstream sibling unless the fork variant has explicit
  semantics elsewhere.
- Literal merge-conflict marker (`<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>`) —
  resolve manually; cargo's syntax error is the only signal.
- Dangling fn ref — either restore the missing fn from `git log -p`
  pre-merge or remove the call site if the upstream refactor obviates
  it.

Re-run `cargo check --workspace` after each batch of fixes until the
exit gate passes.

### Split-commit fallback (only when local Phase 5a is impossible)

If a hard environmental blocker prevents local Phase 5a (e.g. toolchain
install failure, disk-space exhaustion, no Windows SDK staging), split
the rebase into TWO submodule commits and document the split in the
plan + the commit messages:

```bash
# Commit 1 (incomplete — DO NOT push the wrapper gitlink to this SHA alone)
git -C "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched" commit \
  -m "rebase: merge upstream $UPSTREAM_TAG (incomplete)" \
  -m "Phase 5a workspace cargo-check DEFERRED to commit 2 of this pair due to: <concrete blocker>. The wrapper gitlink MUST NOT point at this SHA alone — the workspace may not parse."

# ... resolve the rebase-debt artifacts in the same worktree ...

# Commit 2 (the workspace-green reconciliation)
git -C "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched" commit \
  -m "rebase: post-merge reconciliation (workspace green)" \
  -m "Resolves rebase-debt artifacts surfaced post-merge: <bullet list>. cargo check --workspace exit 0 verified at <SHA>."

# Force-push BOTH commits together (the pair is atomic from the consumer perspective)
git -C "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched" \
  push origin HEAD:sandbox-patches --force-with-lease
```

**Wrapper-side gitlink safety check (Phase 5a invariant — MANDATORY
when the split-commit fallback is used):** before staging the
wrapper-side gitlink bump in step 8, verify the target SHA's tip
commit message does NOT contain the `(incomplete)` marker:

```bash
TARGET_SHA=$(git -C external/repos/codex-patched rev-parse HEAD)
TARGET_MSG=$(git -C external/repos/codex-patched log -1 --format=%s "$TARGET_SHA")
if [[ "$TARGET_MSG" == *"(incomplete)"* ]]; then
  echo "REFUSE: gitlink target $TARGET_SHA is the incomplete commit of a split-commit pair." >&2
  echo "Bump the gitlink only after the post-merge reconciliation commit lands on sandbox-patches." >&2
  exit 1
fi
git add external/repos/codex-patched
```

If the check fails, the workspace would not parse for downstream
consumers; resolve by either advancing `sandbox-patches` to the
reconciliation commit first or by bumping the gitlink to that SHA
explicitly. The split-commit pattern is a fallback, not a default —
single-commit "workspace green at merge time" is preferred whenever
possible.

## Phase 5b — post-push CI closeout

**Phase 5b wraps steps 9-13.** Phase 5b begins after step 8 (wrapper
gitlink bump on the codex wrapper pushed to `gim-home/codex@main` by
the lead's FF-merge) and runs in parallel with steps 9-13 (audit
gates, build, smoke, publish). It is the durable CI-side proof that
the workspace stayed green after the rebase landed for downstream
consumers.

### What runs

`.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml` on `gim-home/codex` triggers on
every push to `main` (and to `codex-patched/**` branches). It checks
out the wrapper with `submodules: recursive`, picks up the new
`external/repos/codex-patched` gitlink, and runs `cargo test
--workspace` from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs` on both
`ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` with a 6-hour timeout. This is the
canonical workspace-coverage signal.

### Exit gate for the rebase task

- The first invariant-check run triggered by the wrapper gitlink bump
  must reach `conclusion: success` on BOTH the Linux and Windows
  matrix legs.
- A `failure` conclusion on either leg surfaces type-drift or test-
  regression that the local Phase 5a missed — see "What to do on CI
  failure" below.
- A `cancelled` / `timed_out` / `startup_failure` conclusion is NOT
  green and does NOT close the rebase task. See "Interim closeout when
  CI is org-policy-blocked" below for the documented exception path.

### How to watch

```bash
# Get the most recent run for the wrapper SHA you just pushed
WRAPPER_SHA="<the SHA from step 8 lead FF-merge>"
gh run list --repo gim-home/codex --workflow invariant-check --limit 5 \
  --json headSha,conclusion,status,databaseId
# wait for the row matching $WRAPPER_SHA to flip from "in_progress" to "completed"
gh run watch <run-id> --repo gim-home/codex --exit-status
```

`gh run watch ... --exit-status` returns non-zero on a failed run,
which makes it scriptable for an autonomous Ralph member.

### What to do on CI failure

If Phase 5a was clean locally but CI surfaces failures, the most likely
causes (in observed-frequency order) are:

1. **Platform-specific drift** — Windows-only fail on Linux-green code
   (or vice versa). Fix in the wrapper worktree's submodule checkout,
   re-verify locally with `cargo check --workspace` AND scoped
   `cargo test -p <crate>` for the affected crate, then **force-push
   on top of `sandbox-patches`** per the skill convention (sandbox-
   patches lives through `--force-with-lease` resets — it is not a
   release branch and does not preserve history outside of the
   `release/<wrapper-version>` retention tags described in
   `CLAUDE.md`):

   ```bash
   git -C "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched" commit \
     -m "rebase-debt-fix: <one-line description>"
   git -C "$REBASE_WORKTREE/external/repos/codex-patched" \
     push origin HEAD:sandbox-patches --force-with-lease
   ```

   Then re-bump the wrapper gitlink in a follow-up wrapper commit AND
   bump the codexu submodule pointer in a small follow-up codexu
   commit — both should reference the same `sandbox-patches` SHA the
   fix landed on. Phase 5b restarts and watches the new CI run.

2. **Rebase-debt missing `#[ignore]` markers** — upstream tests that
   exercise endpoints this fork disables (analytics,
   cloud-requirements, remote_control) need the `#[ignore = "patched
   fork disables ..."]` markers added back per the silent-drop
   checklist in this skill. See the `## Audit gate` section.

3. **Windows-only stack overflows in tracing tests** — pre-existing
   flake; if reproducible on `main` independent of the rebase, file a
   separate task. Do not block the rebase on a non-regression flake,
   but document it in the rebase commit message so future rebases
   recognize it.

### Interim closeout when CI is org-policy-blocked

As of 2026-04-07 every `invariant-check` run on `gim-home/codex@main`
returns `startup_failure` with an empty `jobs` array — the canonical
fingerprint of an org-level GitHub Actions policy rejection at
dispatch time. The block affects ALL workflows on `gim-home/codex`
(invariant-check, publish-npm, Dependabot) and is tracked as
`escalate-gim-home-actions-policy` in codexu `.ralph-overview/data.json`
— operator-only fix at
`https://github.com/organizations/gim-home/settings/actions`.

Until that block lifts, no Phase 5b CI signal is available. The
documented interim-closeout path is:

1. **Phase 5a local cargo-check workspace pass** is the primary green
   signal. The captured `cargo-check-workspace.out` log goes into the
   rebase task's `shipManifest.summary` as the verification evidence.
2. **Local release build pass** (`cargo build --release --bin codex
   --bin codex-core ...` from the build step) is the secondary green
   signal. A successful local build implies the workspace links, not
   just parses.
3. **Local pre-tag runtime smoke pass** (the existing `### Pre-tag
   runtime smoke` section) is the tertiary green signal — actually
   exercises the auth path end-to-end.

If all three pass, the rebase task may flip `lifecycle: merged` with
an explicit `shipManifest.summary` note: `"interim closeout: CI gated
on escalate-gim-home-actions-policy; local Phase 5a + release build +
pre-tag smoke all green; cargo-check-workspace.out at <path>"`. Record
the local cargo-check log path in the manifest as a future-CI-replay
anchor.

### Sunset checklist (self-triggering)

The interim path stays in force only as long as
`escalate-gim-home-actions-policy` blocks the workflow dispatch. When
the bookkeeper-lead observes that task flip to `lifecycle: merged` in
`.ralph-overview/data.json`, the lead executes this concrete
checklist — same turn, before resuming any other work:

1. **Retroactively trigger CI on the most recent
   `gim-home/codex@main` HEAD** via workflow_dispatch:

   ```bash
   WRAPPER_HEAD=$(gh api repos/gim-home/codex/commits/main \
     --jq '.sha')
   gh workflow run invariant-check --repo gim-home/codex --ref main \
     -f head_sha=$WRAPPER_HEAD
   gh run watch $(gh run list --repo gim-home/codex \
     --workflow invariant-check --limit 1 --json databaseId \
     --jq '.[0].databaseId') --repo gim-home/codex --exit-status
   ```

2. **If the retro CI run is green**: amend (or remove) this Phase 5b
   interim-closeout subsection so future rebases follow the real CI
   gate. The minimum edit is to add a note: "Sunset triggered
   <date>: real CI is now the authoritative Phase 5b signal; this
   interim subsection is retained as historical reference only."

3. **If the retro CI run is red**: file a new task to chase the
   regressions (do NOT modify Phase 5b yet — the interim path is
   still load-bearing until CI demonstrably passes once).

4. **Cross-check**: scan every rebase task that closed under the
   interim path (search `.ralph-overview/data.json` for
   `shipManifest.summary` containing `"interim closeout"`); if any
   are still active or need retroactive validation, escalate to the
   operator.

This sunset checklist is also referenced from the
`escalate-gim-home-actions-policy` task entry in
`.ralph-overview/data.json` as a `kanbanCards` row so the bookkeeper
sees it next to the unblock event.
````

## Open Questions

**Q1 [INFERRED] — Phase 5a/5b naming overlap with codexu impl
protocol.** The codexu fork-level `AGENTS.md` already uses "Phase
5a/5b" for the impl-member code-review + docs-review convergence loops
("Every implement-driving spawn prompt must hard-code Phase 5a (code
review-fix convergence) and Phase 5b (docs review-fix convergence)
before fast-forward and push"). This plan introduces the same names
for the codex rebase workflow. **Inferred decision**: keep the name
in both contexts because (a) they share a structural pattern (Phase
5a = "local hard gate", Phase 5b = "external/CI verification"), (b)
the codexu and codex docs are distinct, (c) the cross-ref bullet
makes the distinction explicit via a "Naming overlap warning" callout.
**Confidence: medium**. If the bookkeeper-lead or operator prefers
distinct names (e.g. "Rebase Phase A/B" or "Phase R5a/R5b"), the impl
member can flip naming in one batch — only 3 sections + 4 mirror
bullets need re-titling, and grep can identify every reference.

**Q2 [INFERRED] — Split-commit enforcement layer.** The plan codifies
the split-commit pattern as a fallback and adds a wrapper-side
gitlink safety check that refuses an `(incomplete)`-marker target.
**Inferred decision**: do NOT add a separate CI-level guard in this
task. The grep-based safety check at gitlink-bump time is sufficient
because the wrapper-side step 8 is where the bug would manifest, and
that step IS the protocol section the safety check lives in. If
a second split-commit instance ever bypasses it (e.g. an agent
ignores the check), file a follow-up to add a server-side hook.

**Q3 [INFERRED] — Should `publish-sandbox-patch.md` cross-reference
Phase 5a?** The publish flow already references `cargo check -p
codex-core` (per-crate, not workspace). It does NOT today require
Phase 5a to have run before invocation. **Inferred decision**: don't
modify `publish-sandbox-patch.md` in this task — publish is invoked
AFTER the rebase ships, and the rebase skill is where the gate must
hold. Adding a cross-ref is a small follow-up if we observe publish-
time regressions tracking back to a missed Phase 5a.

**Q4 [INFERRED — accepted Medium per reviewer Cx-M5] — Section size.**
The new Phase 5a + Phase 5b sections are large (~150 LoC total). One
reviewer suggested a shorter overlay that just links to existing
`## Build step`, `## Audit gate`, and `## Pre-tag runtime smoke`
sections. **Inferred decision**: keep the new sections self-contained.
Rationale: future rebase agents will read the skill from scratch in a
fresh context; the "click through three other sections to assemble
the protocol" version is more error-prone than the small duplication
cost. The new sections DO explicitly cross-reference the existing
sections at their tops ("Phase 5a expands step 5; Phase 5b wraps
steps 9-13"), which makes the relationship visible without forcing
the reader to bounce around.

five impl-scope file edits are tightly coupled by lockstep rules

canonical-source-of-truth dependency (the mirror pointers can't be
